beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — open on the Claude composer, ask shown answered; custom greeting for Sanjana; @HumanitariansAI handle in the composer chrome
beats.narration_text: Hi, this is Liam for Sanjana, and this video is about W S J F — Weighted Shortest Job First: the one formula that tells you what to build next.

props.command: claude "rank this product backlog — what should we build next?"
output: scoring: cost of delay ÷ job size

beats.role_note: the stakes, then the framework shown as a STRUCTURE before any example

qc.sparse_reason: Framework card: a single centered equation (WSJF = CoD / Size) + three CoD chips on cream, shown before any example. In 9:16 a centered formula leaves negative space by design, like a title card; edge-bleed and contrast still enforced.

beats.narration_text: Here's the problem. Most backlogs get ordered by whoever argues loudest, or by raw business value, so the biggest, shiniest feature goes first. That's how a team spends a whole quarter shipping the wrong thing. W S J F fixes the order with one idea: value per unit of effort. Weighted Shortest Job First equals Cost of Delay, divided by Job Size. And Cost of Delay is not just business value — it's business value, plus time-criticality, plus risk reduction. Score every item, do the highest first.

props.title: THE FRAMEWORK
props.caption: Score every item. Do the highest first.

beats.role_note: composer — cycle 1 prompt (the shortcut most teams take)
beats.narration_text: Let's build it with Claude. Here's a five-item backlog, each with a business-value score and an effort size in story points. First pass — the shortcut most teams reach for: just rank by value divided by size.

props.command:
claude "score backlog.csv by business_value / job_size,
  then print it ranked high to low"

beats.role_note: ClaudeCodeBeat — the ACTUAL generated code, trimmed to what teaches
beats.narration_text: Read it before you trust it. It loads the backlog, and for each item divides value by size — points of value per point of effort — then sorts high to low. That denominator is the whole trick: at equal value, a cheap item beats an expensive one.

props.title: wsjf.py
props.code:
import csv
rows = list(csv.DictReader(
    open("backlog.csv")))

for r in rows:
    v = int(r["value"])
    size = int(r["size"])
    # CoD = value only (v1)
    r["wsjf"] = v / size

rows.sort(
    key=lambda r: r["wsjf"],
    reverse=True)

beats.role_note: MOVING output — WsjfBoard re-sort, value-only cost of delay
beats.narration_text: Run it, and watch the order flip. The big new onboarding flow — the highest raw value on the board — drops to the middle, because it's an eight-point job. The two-point checkout bug jumps to the top. Same kind of value, a quarter of the cost. That's already smarter than ranking by value alone. But the cost of delay here is still wrong.

props.title: PASS 1 · VALUE ÷ SIZE
props.caption: Cheap beats expensive at equal value.

beats.narration_text: Here's the check. Cost of delay is not just business value. A security fix can be low value but high urgency and high risk — and value-over-size buries it. So iterate: cost of delay equals value, plus time-criticality, plus risk reduction. Re-rank.

props.command:
claude "update wsjf.py:
  cost_of_delay = value + time_criticality + risk_reduction
  then re-rank"

beats.narration_text: One line changes. Cost of delay becomes a sum of three: how much users want it, how fast its value decays, and how much risk it burns down. Divide that by size, and sort again.

props.title: wsjf.py
props.code:
for r in rows:
    value = int(r["value"])
    # delay has three costs:
    tc = int(
      r["time_criticality"])
    rr = int(
      r["risk_reduction"])
    cod = value + tc + rr
    size = int(r["size"])
    r["wsjf"] = cod / size
props.sparkLine: Delay has three costs, not one.

beats.role_note: MOVING output — WsjfBoard re-sort, full cost of delay; the change made visible
beats.narration_text: Re-run. Now API rate limiting — low business value, but urgent and risky — leaps from near the bottom to number two. Nothing about the work changed; we just stopped pretending value was the only cost of waiting. That is the ranking you actually act on.

props.title: PASS 2 · FULL COST OF DELAY
props.caption: Urgency and risk are costs too.

beats.narration_text: So the method is one formula you can run on any backlog: cost of delay — value, time-criticality, risk — over job size, highest first. Two honest limits. W S J F is blind to dependencies: if a low-score task blocks a high-score one, you do the blocker first, score be damned. And the ranking is only as good as the numbers you feed it — garbage estimates, garbage order. So score as a team, not alone.

props.title: THE METHOD
props.caption: Cost of delay ÷ size. Highest first.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — suggested prompt typed in, read aloud and discussed; addressed to Sanjana
beats.narration_text: Your turn, Sanjana. Take your real backlog — a sheet with value, time-criticality, risk, and size — paste this prompt, and let Claude rank it. Then argue with the order. Every place your gut disagrees with the score is a number you need to re-estimate, or a dependency the formula can't see. That argument is the actual planning.

props.command:
claude "here's my backlog.csv (name, value, time_criticality,
  risk_reduction, size). Compute WSJF = (value + time_criticality
  + risk_reduction) / size, rank it, and flag any pair where a
  lower-ranked item blocks a higher one."
